1.1: 1.1 Argument. He makes plain the account of the Word, and that God himself is charity, and discusses how the whisperers among the brothers can neither know God nor become devout, to the point of proving them murderers, because hatred is the occasion of killing. What was from the beginning. In nature, or in the true being of the Godhead, what we have heard, through the law and the prophets, what we have seen, a man visibly coming, what we have looked upon, perceiving the Divinity in the man, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life: not agreeing by chance with him who was seen in the flesh, but with much handling of the Scriptures giving testimony of the Word himself. What someone has seen he can announce to others, what he has once perfectly beheld he cannot explain in words.
1.2: 1.2 We have seen and are witnesses. We have seen, and in announcing to unbelievers have become martyrs. We announce to you. So through them we have heard, but have not seen, yet we are no less blessed than they, because it is written: Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed, Luke 24.
1.5: 1.5 And this is the announcement. Why was the Word made flesh? What new thing did he bring to the world? Why did he come to suffer? It was not in vain; see what he wished to teach, that God is light. By this sentence he shows the excellence of divine purity, which we are commanded to imitate. Hence the Manichaeans are refuted, who say that the nature of God was conquered and corrupted in war by the prince of darkness. We announce, etc. We have drawn near: light has shone upon us toward the light. We were darkness, now through the light we are light, and we enlighten others while we announce that sins are forgiven and darkness expelled.
1.6: 1.6 If we say. So far the commendation of the epistle; here he shows how charity is to be had. And in darkness, etc. Those who persist in sins and darken others are not counted among his members; hence: What agreement has Christ with Belial? What fellowship has light with darkness? II Corinthians 6.
1.7: 1.7 But if in the light. We are clean if we walk in the light, yet we must not think that as long as we live we can be wholly cleansed from sins. As he also, etc. God is said to be in the light because the highest goodness finds nowhere that it could advance, man walks in the light because by works of virtue he advances toward better things.
1.8: 1.8 If we say, etc. Those also lack charity who, proud of their merits, say they are clean. We have. He does not say, we had: lest it might seem said of the past.
1.9: 1.9 He will forgive us our sins. What is graver in us he calls sins, but the lesser he calls iniquity.
1.10: 1.10 A liar. God alone is truthful of himself: man is truthful from God, a liar of himself. It is impossible for any holy person never to fall into the smallest sins. Nor do the just cease to be just, because they rise again the sooner with God's help.
2.1: 2.1 My little children, I write these things, etc. That you may not take on a false security, hearing that you are cleansed by God, but may have a useful fear. If anyone sins. If from human frailty you cannot guard against all vices, take care at least to guard against the greater and more open ones, so that no temptation seize you except a human one. But if anyone even after my warning falls, let him not despair. Advocate. There is no advocate except for those who call on him. Let your sins displease you, cry out: and he hears and frees. Just. A just advocate does not take up unjust causes, yet he will defend us as just in the judgment if we now accuse ourselves as unjust.
2.3: 2.3 And by this we know. To know or recognize is not always said on account of acquaintance, but on account of experience and union with another thing. We know God when we are united to him. He who so knows keeps his commandments. If we keep his commandments. We ought to attend to our frailty, we ought to seek an advocate in sins, and to obtain this we should labor to keep the commandments, by which one comes to the knowledge of him.
2.4: 2.4 He who says he knows, etc. It is no great thing to know one God, since even the demons believe and tremble.
2.7: 2.7 Not a new commandment. The same charity is an old commandment, because it was commended from the beginning. It is the same a new commandment, because when the darkness is cast out it pours in the desire of a new light.
2.8: 2.8 Which is true. According as he promised that by keeping God's commandments one comes to his knowledge and love. And in him. Fulfilled in Christ, because he obeyed the Father even to death: and therefore was glorified. And in you. Some of whom already by this glory with God, and it is truly new because the darkness has already passed. Darkness belongs to the old man, light to the new man.
2.9: 2.9 He who says, etc. He determines what commandment he means, that is charity, and how this charity is to be had, namely the love of God and neighbor.
2.10: 2.10 He who loves his brother is in the light of knowledge and of action; but he who hates is in the darkness of ignorance, and through that ignorance goes from vice to vice, and does not know, that is, does not foresee, where he goes; and to what punishment he is to be taken. Or, he does not know where he goes, that is he is ignorant of the way by which he may be converted to the better, and this not as if the way were not open, but because the darkness has blinded his eyes, who, leaving the light of Christ, is so hindered by sins and carnal pleasure that even if he sees the good, he does not follow it.
2.12: 2.12 I write to you, etc. He puts first a cause that could draw them away from love of the world, because for those baptized in the name of Christ and invoking the name of Christ sins are forgiven, therefore Christ is to be clung to more than the world. Little children. Fathers, young men, youths. Therefore children: because sins are forgiven. Therefore fathers, because you have known the ancient things. Therefore youths, because strong, because you have conquered.
2.13: 2.13 Young men. The time of youth is slippery on account of the incentives of the flesh; but on account of the strength of age it is fit for the contest, and these overcame the temptations of pleasures by love of the word of God, and despised persecutions.
2.14: 2.14 And you have conquered. In that time young men were drawn by custom to the brothel, but these by manfully resisting conquered.
2.15: 2.15 Do not love the world. Use the world for need, but do not love it for superfluity. And take no care of the flesh in its desires. Do not love the world. One heart does not contain two loves that are adversaries to it. Rooted in charity, build nothing upon this root except what agrees with charity, because you cannot serve two masters. As the love of God is the fountain of all virtues, so the love of the world is of all vices.
2.16: 2.16 Everything that is in the world. BEDE. That is: All lovers of the world have nothing but these three, by which, etc., down to he would not be lifted up above the kingdoms of the world.
2.17: 2.17 But he who does the will, etc. In this way also charity can be had, if indeed by no instigation of heretics you have been cast down from the faith and from the other things which are of God. And that you may hold it, let what you heard from the beginning remain in you.
2.18: 2.18 Little children, it is the last hour. And therefore you must persist, because there are many antichrists who wish to seduce you. As you have heard that Antichrist is coming. For with what force and terror you have heard that Antichrist will come, with so much violence these also come. We are in the eleventh hour, the Savior has come in the flesh, and the pestilence of Antichrist is to follow, who will attack the proclamations of salvation, who will root out the vineyard that Christ cultivates, and many members of this wicked head have already been sent ahead, whom we must beware of, because the end of the age is now imminent; or the last hour, that is like the last, this persecution is like that future one. Now there are many antichrists. Antichrists are all heretics, all who destroy by deeds the faith they confess in words; all who are contrary to Christ, who give testimony to their coming head, because the mystery of iniquity is already working in them.
2.19: 2.19 They went out from us, etc. Although there are many antichrists, let it not terrify you if they have returned to Judaism or paganism, do not think that the Church suffers any loss from this; because if they went out from us, yet they were not truly of us. They could not have gone out unless they were opposed to Christ. He who is not opposed to Christ remains in the body of Christ. They are in the Church as bad humors in the body; when they are vomited out, the body is relieved; so when the wicked go out, the Church is relieved. But that they might be made manifest. Many who are not of us receive the sacraments of Christ with us, but temptation proves that they are not of us. When temptation comes to them, as if on the occasion of a wind they fly outside, because they were not grain. All will then fly away, when the Lord's threshing floor begins to be winnowed on the day of judgment. Therefore, with God's permission, some go out of the Church before the final division, showing that they were not of the body of Christ, so that it may be plainly clear that not all are of us who, placed within with us, receive the sacraments of Christ, and therefore their separation ought not to burden you.
2.20: 2.20 But you have an anointing. When he was speaking of heretics, suddenly turning to his own he says they have an anointing from the Holy One, to show on the contrary that heretics and all antichrists are deprived of the gift of spiritual grace, and do not belong to him who is called the Holy One by the prophets. You know all things. You know the truth of faith and of life, taught by the anointing of the Spirit, and have no need to be taught, except to persist in what you have begun.
2.21: 2.21 And because every lie. BEDE. He had said that every lie is not of the truth, etc., down to of all who scorn to obey the commandments of Christ.
2.22: 2.22 This is Antichrist, etc. Behold, we have been told how to recognize Antichrist, namely whoever denies Christ, etc. He who denies the Father. In vain does he confess God the Father who denies the Son, who proceeds from God.
2.24: 2.24 What you have heard, etc. If anyone says: Behold, here is Christ, behold there, do not believe, but hold to what you have heard from the apostles. And you in the Son and the Father. So you will be members of the Father and the Son, so that you do not fall from the memory and protection of the Father and the Son, and this you ought to seek, that you be in the Father and the Son, because from this you will obtain the reward.
2.25: 2.25 This is the promise. May the memory of the promised reward make you persevere in work.
2.27: 2.27 But as his anointing. That is the Holy Spirit, whose sacrament is in the visible anointing; or the anointing of charity is understood, which is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us; which inflames the heart that it fills to keep the commandments of God.
2.28: 2.28 And now, little children, abide. By repeating he presses it, to fix it more tightly in their minds. Abide in him. And if you have any good, impute the whole to him and not to yourselves; impute evils to yourselves and the devil.
2.29: 2.29 Everyone, etc. BEDE. Perfect righteousness is scarcely in the angels, etc., down to when there will be no struggle with the flesh, but triumph over the enemy. From him. If now we are born of the just one, we ought to follow the righteousness of the just Father.
3.1: 3.1 See, etc. Observe carefully with how many and what great gifts God has shown his fatherly charity toward us. For he gave that in this age we should be named children of God by name and deed, and in the future be so, possessing the inherited blessedness. He gave. For this God gave charity that we may know and be able to love him, not however as a servant loves his lord, but as a son his father. Hence it is said: But to as many as received him, he gave power to become children of God, John 1.
3.2: 3.2 We are children of God. As if to say: To be and be called children of God, what a dignity is this? He answers: Beloved, now we are children of God. Now by the miracles we do and by the purity of our life it appears that we are children of God, but whatever it is in the present is little in regard to the future. We shall be like him. For when we enjoy the contemplation of the immutable and eternal Divinity, we too shall be immortal and eternal in him: not indeed the same as he, but like, because we are creatures and made in his likeness. For we shall see. As the Word was made flesh, the wicked have seen him and will see him in the judgment: but as the Word was in the beginning with the Father, the just alone will see him: the wicked will be taken away that he not see the glory of God.
3.3: 3.3 Sanctifies himself. BEDE. He does not take away free will when he says, etc., down to saying to God: You are my helper, do not forsake me, Psalm 26.
3.4: 3.4 And sin, etc. THE SAME. What the Latins call law, the Greeks, etc., down to those who corrupt the innocence of the natural law are guilty of transgression.
3.5: 3.5 And you know. Lest we (who cannot be without sins and iniquities) despair of salvation, he adds that through Christ we are released from sins. Not only then have we been made children of God by grace, and hope that we shall be like him, but we are also freed from iniquity: because he appeared in order to take away sins, from which iniquity no one should excuse himself.
3.6: 3.6 He who sins has not seen him. And he who abides in him does not sin. And in this let no one seduce you, by saying that either righteousness is from man, or that anyone can abide in God with sin, because all righteousness is from God and all sin from the devil.
3.7: 3.7 He who does righteousness. That is: he who has the act and intention of righteousness is indeed righteous, but not of himself: but as that one is, he proceeds from the same root. Righteousness is in that one principally, in this one secondarily, in that one naturally, in this one by adoption. The very fact that he who is righteous is righteous from him.
3.8: 3.8 Is of the devil. BEDE. Not by drawing origin of the flesh, as Manichaeus wished, etc., down to Christ was born man, to loose the sins of men, to lead them back to life.
3.9: 3.9 Does not commit sin. He does not speak of every sin: for if we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, but of the violation of charity, which he who has in himself the seed of God, that is the word of God by which he was reborn, cannot commit. For his seed. The true Son of the Father cannot abandon the law. The law of the Father is: Love one another.
3.12: 3.12 Because his works were evil. Where there is envy there is not brotherly love. He does not call Cain's works evil but envy and hatred of his brother. He does not call Abel's works just but charity. By this men are distinguished. Let no one look at tongues but at deeds. If the heart does not do good for his brothers, it shows what it has in itself. Cain offered rightly, creature to Creator, but he did not divide rightly, when he believed the gifts he offered would please with hatred of his brother. Abel offered with love, and pleased.
3.14: 3.14 We know, etc. Let no one falsely exalt himself over virtues, let no one fear beyond measure the poverty of his strength. He who loves his brother gives clear proof that he belongs to the lot of the just. Remains in death. The life of the flesh is the soul, the life of the soul is God; the death of the body is to lose the spirit; the death of the soul is to lose God. He therefore who through hatred of his brother loses God loses life.
3.15: 3.15 He who hates his brother. He who from hatred pursues his brother provokes him to anger and discord, and so as far as he is concerned kills him in the soul. If anyone scorns hatred of a brother, will he not scorn murder in his heart? He does not move his hands to kill, and he is already held a murderer: that one lives, and this one is judged a slayer. He does not have eternal life. Forever, he will be condemned with Cain, who is held guilty of this kind of murder, that he is at discord with his brothers.
3.16: 3.16 In this we know, etc. Having set forth many reasons for having charity, at last he adds about the perfection of charity, under the example of the Lord's passion. Peter is admonished to have this, when to the Lord asking he professed that he loved, to whom it is said: But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not wish, John 21. In which words he was taught to lay down his life for the sheep. For greater love than this no one has, that one lay down his life for his friends, ibid. 15.
3.17: 3.17 Whoever has, etc. If, whether by the opportuneness of the time or by human infirmity, it does not happen that we lay down our lives, we ought at least to lay down our goods for our brothers, and this is the nourishment of charity. He who has learned to give his property will some day be able to lay down himself.
3.18: 3.18 Little children, let us not love, etc. Because charity is not perfect in him who does not lay down his life for his brothers, or who at least does not give money. Therefore that you may have perfect charity, little children of the same father. Let us not love in word, nor in tongue. In word is understood pure speech, not work; in tongue, multiplied speech, as some, by often repeated discourses, wish to commend their affection. But in deed. Because even if we are deceived in love through human infirmity, we are not deceived in the reward, because God is greater than our heart, and knows with what zeal all things are done. And in truth. If we bestow benefits with a simple intention, not for boasting or for some temporal advantage, but with respect to God alone.
3.19: 3.19 In this we know, etc. In this that we love the truth, we know that we are of the truth, that is we know that we have this true love from God (who is truth), and from this love we know that we are in his sight, that is we merit his sight, and in this also we persuade our hearts to think out better works. And in his sight, etc. That is, we persuade our hearts to have such thoughts as are worthy of divine sight. For all who propose to do something turn their hearts to meditate on the same deed. But he who thinks evil, if he could, would hide it from God: but those who think good persuade their hearts most easily to desire that it be laid open to the sight of God, which is a sign of great perfection, when one's own work or thought delights to be seen by God.
3.20: 3.20 For if he reproves. And this is great that through love we have our thoughts so clean that we wish to show them to God: for even if conscience accused us within and wished to hide from God, because we did our good not with a good spirit, still we could not hide from God, because he is greater than our heart and knows all things: love is therefore powerful, which commends us to him from whom we cannot be hidden.
3.22: 3.22 And whatever we ask. A great promise and desirable to the faithful. But if anyone is so perverse that he is not delighted with heavenly promises, let him at least fear what wisdom on the contrary thunders terribly: He who turns away his ear that he may not hear the law, his prayer will be execrable, Proverbs 28.
3.23: 3.23 And this is the commandment. He puts the commandment first in the singular, and adds two, because these cannot be separated.
4.1: 4.1 Because many. Many heretics, many schismatics confess that Jesus came in the flesh, but by their deeds they deny it, in not having charity. By charity the Word was made flesh; he who does not have charity denies that he came in the flesh, and so is convicted of not having the Spirit from God. The Spirit of God says that Jesus came in the flesh not by the sound of the tongue but by loving and doing. Jesus came to gather, the heretic scatters: he does not have the Spirit of God.
4.3: 4.3 Every spirit, etc. Many heretics, who wished to separate the unity of the Church by a perverse doctrine, erased this little verse from the epistle, so as not to be convicted of error by it. Dissolves. He who distinguishes God from man, who divides the members from God, who badly interprets the words of God, who departs from God by living badly, he dissolves Jesus.
4.5: 4.5 They are of the world. These spirits that are of the world are not to be loved, not to be heard. Because even if they invoke the name of Christ and mark themselves with the sign of Christ, yet they are of the number of those who desire worldly things, who know not heavenly things. Therefore they speak of the world. By the reason of worldly wisdom proving that God cannot raise a dead man, that a mortal man cannot have a dwelling in heaven, and the like.
4.7: 4.7 Beloved, let us love one another. He has commended charity in many ways, now he comes to its singular praise in which we ought especially to hear him, namely: He who loves is born of God and knows God, because God is charity. He had said: Charity is of God; here he added: God is charity.
4.8: 4.8 Because God is charity. Charity does not differ in God, when he is called just and justice, loving and love, because he is called just or loving not by a transferred name from justice or love, as if he had justice or love distinct from himself, but because he is his own justice and love.
4.9: 4.9 In this appeared. Proving that God is charity and that he loves us, he wished to lead us by his example to love one another and come to his knowledge. As God did not wait for us to love him, so let us not wait for others to love us, but love first. The Father's love was proved because he sent the Son: the Son's love appeared in this, that he died for us whom he loved beforehand.
4.10: 4.10 Not as if we. We did not first love, as if by the merit of our love he loved us, but he first loved us, that by his grace going before we may love him.
4.11: 4.11 And we ought to love one another. Love, and do what you will. Whether you keep silent, keep silent out of love: whether you cry out, cry out out of love. From this root nothing but good can come.
4.12: 4.12 No one has ever seen God. BEDE. As these visible things are seen, known by the senses of the body, so God is not seen, etc., down to while we are still pilgrims in the body, let us love one another, etc.
4.13: 4.13 In this we know. How shall we know whether we have the Spirit of God? Ask your own heart: if it is full of charity, you have the Spirit of God. Because we abide in him. God abides in us, and we in him, and therefore let no one despair of salvation, because even if the diseases of crimes press us down, the physician is almighty and will save. Let us rejoice in hope that we may come to the reality.
4.16: 4.16 And we have known. We have seen and testify that God sent his Son, and we have known for what cause he did this: not because he needed, not because he owed anything, but by charity alone. Though he had an only Son he did not wish him to be alone, but that he might have brothers, and adopted for him those who would possess eternal life with him.
4.18: 4.18 There is no fear in charity. In that charity, namely, which in imitation of the divine goodness does good even to enemies, there is no fear.
5.1: 5.1 Everyone who believes. He believes who so lives as Christ commanded, otherwise the demons also believe. But works without faith are either nothing, or, even if they seem good, are empty, because they are apart from the way, which is Christ. Truly he who loves God loves his brother. For he who loves God the Father loves God the Son, begotten of the Father, and he who loves God the Son loves also the children of God, members of that head.
5.3: 5.3 Are not heavy. BEDE. They do not drag downward, like a talent of lead, etc., down to lest anyone trust in his own strength that he can overcome the world, he adds about faith:
5.4: 5.4 And this is the victory, etc. That faith, to be sure, which works through love, which asks the help of God.
5.5: 5.5 Who is it? etc. He determines which faith conquers, namely the faith of Christ. As if: Truly it overcomes the world by faith, because it is not overcome by anything else. Our faith. Behold which faith conquers, that which believes him true man and true God.
5.6: 5.6 This is, etc. Because faith alone and confession of divinity does not suffice for salvation and for overcoming the world, he adds also about the humanity: therefore he expressed the blood. Spirit. That is the human soul which he sent forth in the passion; water and blood, which flowed from the side. This could not be if he had not the true nature of flesh. But even before the passion, the sweat which became like drops of blood shows the truth of the flesh. And that from the side of one already dead, contrary to nature, water and blood flowed vividly, testified that the body of the Lord would live better after death, and his death would give life to us. That the sweat flowed to the earth like blood signified that with his blood he would wash the Church throughout the whole world.
5.7: 5.7 Because there are three. By this it appears that Jesus is truth, true God, true man. And of both we have sure testimony, of the Godhead through the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit: of the humanity through soul, water, and blood. The Father gave testimony of the Godhead when he said: This is my beloved Son. The Son himself gave it when he was transfigured on the mountain, and showed the power of the Divinity and the hope of eternal blessedness. The Holy Spirit gave it when he rested on the baptized in the form of a dove, or when at the invocation of the name of Christ he filled the hearts of believers.
5.10: 5.10 He who believes in the Son of God. He understands the Father to be truthful in testimony of the Son. He who does not believe says the Father is a liar. In vain therefore do the Jews say they believe in the Father, as long as they despise Christ. In the Son. Because the Father testifies of the Son, let us believe in the Son. Because he who so believes in the Son that by good desire he tends toward him has the testimony of God in himself, as if to say: God testifies also of this, that he who so believes will be in the number of the children of God, the Son himself so promising his own: If anyone serves me, my Father will honor him, John 12. If therefore you have God as witness of your faith, what does the infamy or persecution of men hurt you? If God is for us, who is against us? Romans 8.
5.11: 5.11 And this is the testimony. He testified of the Son, and also of us adopted sons, that through his only Son he would give eternal life also to us, now in hope, but in due time in reality. And this is life. BEDE. In faith and confession of the name, in receiving the sacraments, etc., down to who gives his own eternal life.
5.14: 5.14 And this is the confidence. In many ways he presses the same things he had promised above, to rouse us more lively to prayer. According to his will. By which he wishes that we ask what he wills, or that we come to ask as such as he desires us to be. If we want our salvation and that of our neighbors we do not disagree with the will of God. If our will through ignorance departs from the will of God, the good will of God corrects our foolish one, as happened to the apostle Paul.
5.15: 5.15 We know that, etc. Because we know that we have from him the petitions we ask, let us ask nothing that is against him, nothing except what he has taught us, what he has inspired in us: and if we err in any way, we are straightway corrected.
5.16: 5.16 He who knows his brother. BEDE. He speaks of daily and light sins, etc., down to and by the examination of them chastise yourself. There is a sin unto death. This sin separates from God, as death separates the soul from the body.
5.17: 5.17 All iniquity is sin. As if: Prayer is truly to be made for those sinning not unto death, because all are occupied with many sins, and no one can be without sin, because all iniquity is sin. But above, there is another sin unto death, which is not committed by human frailty, and therefore is not purged by the prayer of the just: because those who do such things will not obtain the kingdom of God.
5.18: 5.18 Everyone who is born, etc. He who is born of God does not sin unto death: he who is not born, sins; but we are of those who are born of God: therefore we shall not sin, we shall not be touched by the enemy, but lovers of the world are subject to the evil enemy. Does not sin. David sinned gravely, but because born of God he belonged to the company of the children of God, he did not sin unto death, but by penance he merited pardon. But the generation of God, etc. Those who persevere in the generation of God cannot sin, nor be touched by the evil one. As day and night cannot be mingled, so righteousness and iniquity, the evil one and the generation of God. The evil one therefore touches some, hurting and afflicting, but not to their harm.
5.19: 5.19 And the whole world. Not only lovers of the world, but also the newly born, who do not have discernment of good and evil, belong to the kingdom of the devil on account of the first transgression, unless they are rescued by the grace of God from the darkness.
5.20: 5.20 And we know, etc. No one without divine knowledge can come to eternal life, no one can know without the grace of God, because no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and to whom the Son wishes to reveal both the Father and the Son. For the Son reveals both, who appearing visible in the flesh made known the secrets of the Divinity to the world through the Gospel.
5.21: 5.21 Little children. And because you know the true God and true man, and await eternal life, keep yourselves from the doctrines of heretics, who take on the appearance of holiness, who by perverse dogmas change the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of corruptible things. For avarice is the service of idols; those therefore who prefer the world to God are idolaters. Keep. Though he had given testimony of their perfection in many things, it could yet be feared that some newly converted might retain in mind remnants of superstition, and therefore he shows that the worship of idols is to be fled.
